title: Energy-Efficient Deep Learning Without Backpropagation: A Rigorous Hardware-Validated Benchmarking Study of Forward-Only Algorithms
abstract: arXiv:2511.01061v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Backpropagation (BP) powers modern deep learning, but it must hold every activation in memory until a global backward sweep consumes it, and that sweep locks each layer until the one above has finished. Forward-only algorithms, from Hinton's Forward-Forward (FF) through Cascaded Forward (CaFo) to Mono-Forward (MF), replace the global gradient with local learning signals and are promoted as more efficient on the basis of FLOP counts rather than measurements. We test that claim on hardware. Across almost 1000 runs on four vision benchmarks (MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100), we read energy, power and memory from an NVIDIA A100 GPU and compare each algorithm against a tuned BP baseline. Removing the backward pass does not by itself save energy: FF costs 4.1x to 6.3x BP's energy and CaFo 3.0x to 7.1x. Mono-Forward is the exception. Given the same number of data passes as BP, it uses 12.5% to 19.9% less energy and 24.6%

translated_title: 无反向传播的能效深度学习：仅前向算法的严格硬件验证基准测试研究
translated_abstract: 反向传播驱动着现代深度学习，但它必须将每个激活值保留在内存中，直到全局的反向扫描将其消耗，且该扫描会锁定每一层，直到其上一层完成计算。仅前向算法——从Hinton的前向-前向算法，到级联前向，再到单向前向——用局部学习信号取代了全局梯度，并被基于FLOP计算量而非实际测量的方式宣传为更加高效。我们在硬件上对这一说法进行了检验。在四个视觉基准数据集（MNIST、Fashion-MNIST、CIFAR-10和CIFAR-100）上进行了近1000次运行，我们从NVIDIA A100 GPU上读取能耗、功率和内存数据，并将每种算法与经过调优的BP基线进行比较。结果表明，移除反向传播本身并不能节省能量：FF的能耗是BP的4.1倍至6.3倍，CaFo为3.0倍至7.1倍。Mono-Forward是唯一的例外。在与BP相同的数据遍历次数下，它节省了12.5%至19.9%的能耗和24.6%的（原文在此截断）
tldr: 该研究首次在真实硬件（NVIDIA A100 GPU）上对仅前向学习算法进行了严格的能效基准测试，发现大多数前向算法（FF、CaFo）的实际能耗反而高于反向传播，唯有Mono-Forward算法在相同训练条件下实现了12.5%至19.9%的节能。
en_tdlr: This study provides the first rigorous hardware-validated energy benchmarking of forward-only learning algorithms on an NVIDIA A100 GPU, revealing that most forward-only algorithms (FF, CaFo) actually consume more energy than backpropagation, while Mono-Forward uniquely achieves 12.5% to 19.9% energy savings under equal training conditions.
